title: Scout Pane — Global Surface Index & Rollout Layering
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Prototype and validate a single, persistent global surface ("Scout Pane") that centralizes workspace switching, route discovery, rollout status, and cost lenses. The Scout Pane will be the canonical entrypoint for cross-workspace routing and operational context, designed to reduce cognitive load for power users and to surface rollout/rollbacks and cost hotspots without leaving the current flow.

Scope: IA and visual system for the Scout Pane across desktop widths >= 1000px; mobile behavior out-of-scope for this ticket (see DES-86744). Includes: persistent left-hand panel variant, compact overlay variant, keyboard-first navigation, quick-action affordances (pin route, open rollout preview, jump to cost report), and telemetry hooks for per-route time-to-task and abandonment.

Design principles: progressive disclosure (start with workspace and 6 most-used routes), frictionless switching (single keystroke to jump), low visual noise for non-admins (role-aware controls), and explicit rollout awareness (canary, A/B, fallback) with clear CTAs to follow rollout runbooks. Emphasis on performance for orgs with 100+ workspaces (virtualized lists, server-side workspace sampling).

Outcomes expected: improved route discovery metrics, reduction in workspace-switch latency, clearer operator awareness of rollouts that affect user-facing routes, and direct shortcuts to cost-lens drilldowns to reduce time-to-insight for high-spend paths.
notes: 2025-02-11: Kickoff review with PM and Eng. Agreement to keep Scout Pane persistent on desktop; overlay for constrained widths. Action: design to produce two prototypes (persistent left rail + transient omnibox).
2025-02-18: Wireframes v1 posted to Figma. Note from Eng (Aisha Malik): need virtualization strategy for workspace list and prefetching of rollout state to avoid spikes. Added ENG-2398 as dependency.

2025-02-21: Internal design critique: reduce iconography and rely on color tokens for rollout severity; add accessible labels for color-blind modes. Action: create high-contrast variant and ARIA spec for keyboard focus states.

2025-02-25: Prototype (persistent) uploaded: figma link below. Usability test scheduled 2025-02-28 with 6 engineers and 4 product managers — tasks centered on switching to a route under an active canary and finding cost hotspots for that route.

2025-03-01: Usability summary: mean time-to-switch dropped 32% in prototype vs baseline; 2 participants confused by rollout pill semantics (canary vs full) — need clearer microcopy and hover detail. Added microcopy iteration and tooltip patterns.

2025-03-03: PM feedback (Eleanor Cho): prioritize rollout preview CTA and add an inline 'open runbook' button for high-risk rollouts. Also request: surface estimated per-minute cost for top 3 routes via a lightweight API call. Added ENG-2345 for cost API contract.

2025-03-04: Design updated with microcopy, added fallback affordance and 'revert to stable' quick action for users with operator role. Ready for handoff to Eng for spike implementation of virtualization and rollout-state caching.
design_decisions: Persistent left pane chosen for power-users to minimize context-switching; overlay reserved for low-width and first-time flows.
Virtualize workspace list and cache rollout metadata server-side to avoid client load; team agreed to an API that returns paged workspace descriptors with recent routes and rollout summaries.
Role-aware controls: non-admins see a read-only rollout indicator; admins get quick-actions (open rollout, rollback, open runbook).
Cost lens: embed a lightweight 'cost snapshot' (3 routes) in the pane using a pre-aggregated endpoint to avoid heavy queries. Full cost drilldown links to the Cost Dashboard.
Accessibility: keyboard-first traversal (Cmd/Ctrl+K opens omnibox; arrow keys to navigate; Enter to jump), ARIA live regions for rollout state changes, and color-contrast compliant tokens.
open_questions: How should multi-tenant RBAC map to quick-actions — strict enforcement client-side or server validation with lazy UI hints? (PM leaning: server validation only)
What is acceptable eventual consistency window for cached rollout state? (Eng suggests 30s; PM requested 10s for critical paths)
Should cost snapshot include last-24h or last-60m delta? (sprint callout to measure both in telemetry)
Mobile/compact pattern: overlay vs bottom-sheet — deferred to DES-86744 prototype.
acceptance_criteria: Figma persistent-pane and overlay prototypes delivered with annotations for ARIA and keyboard interactions
Eng spike accepted demonstrating virtualization approach and rollout-state caching (proof-of-concept in staging)
Microcopy iteration addressing canary/full rollout confusion validated in follow-up usability test (n>=5)
API contracts for cost snapshot and rollout summary signed off by ENG and PM
Telemetry events defined for route-switch, rollout-preview-open, cost-snapshot-click to measure adoption
next_steps: Handoff meeting with ENG on 2025-03-06 to align on API shape and virtualization strategy
PM to add cost API work to backlog and confirm SLA for snapshot freshness
Design to produce a compact overlay variant for mobile (DES-86744) and an accessibility spec doc
Schedule follow-up usability test after Eng spike completes (target 2025-03-18)
